## What it is

This is **eShop** — a .NET reference microservices e-commerce application, orchestrated by **.NET Aspire**. The analyzer classifies it as an App (not a library) with a **Microservices** style at high confidence, on evidence of "Aspire orchestration of 9 runnable services" (`eShop.slnx`, 19 projects). The stack is net10.0, Minimal APIs + MVC controllers, MediatR/CQRS, EF Core, FluentValidation, and DDD aggregates (`Order`, `Buyer`).

Note there are **3 solutions on disk**; the one analyzed is `eShop.slnx`. The other two are `src/ClientApp/ClientApp.sln` and `tests/ClientApp.UnitTests/ClientApp.UnitTests.sln`.

## The single entry point you run

**`src/eShop.AppHost`** is the Aspire AppHost and the only thing you launch. It is the root of the dependency graph (in-degree 0, out-degree 9) and it composes everything else.

## Processes the AppHost starts

Nine .NET processes, each registered in `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs`:

| Process | Kind | Registered at |
|---|---|---|
| **Identity.API** | IdentityServer (Duende) auth provider | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:23` |
| **Basket.API** | gRPC service | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:30` |
| **Catalog.API** | Web API (EF Core + pgvector) | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:36` |
| **Ordering.API** | Web API (EF Core, MediatR, FluentValidation) | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:40` |
| **OrderProcessor** | Worker service | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:46` |
| **PaymentProcessor** | Worker service | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:51` |
| **Webhooks.API** | Web API | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:54` |
| **WebhookClient** | Blazor UI | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:65` |
| **WebApp** | Blazor storefront (+ YARP) | `src/eShop.AppHost/Program.cs:69` |

The AppHost also applies a cross-cutting hook that sets `ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true` on every project resource (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:22`, `src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:32-40`), and wires an AI backend for Catalog.API and WebApp — either OpenAI/Azure OpenAI (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:51`) or a containerized **Ollama** with OpenWebUI plus `all-minilm` embedding and `llama3.1` chat models (`src/eShop.AppHost/Extensions.cs:163-172`).

## Backing infrastructure resources

The services resolve Aspire resources by name, so the AppHost also brings up:
- **Redis** as `"redis"` — Basket.API's store (`src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:14-16`)
- **RabbitMQ** as `"eventbus"` — the shared bus (`src/Basket.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:18`, `src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:31`, `src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:10`)
- **PostgreSQL** databases — `"catalogdb"` with the vector extension (`src/Catalog.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:15-21`) and `"orderingdb"` (`src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:13`)

I did not read `Program.cs` directly (the tooling exposed only graph provenance for it, not its text), so the exact lines where these containers are declared are inferred from the consuming services plus the `Aspire.Hosting.PostgreSQL`, `Aspire.Hosting.Redis`, `Aspire.Hosting.RabbitMQ` and `Aspire.Hosting.Yarp` package references. I also did not verify the database resource names used by Identity.API and Webhooks.API.

## Not started by the AppHost

**ClientApp** (.NET MAUI) and **HybridApp** (.NET MAUI + Blazor WebView) are runnable clients but are *not* among the AppHost's nine dependencies — you launch them separately onto a device/emulator. ClientApp has its own solution at `src/ClientApp/ClientApp.sln`.

Supporting libraries with no process of their own: `eShop.ServiceDefaults`, `EventBus`, `EventBusRabbitMQ`, `IntegrationEventLogEF`, `Ordering.Domain`, `Ordering.Infrastructure`, `WebAppComponents`.

## How the processes talk

- **WebApp → Basket.API** over gRPC (`src/WebApp/Services/BasketService.cs:7` → `src/Basket.API/Grpc/BasketService.cs:8`)
- **WebApp → Catalog.API / Ordering.API** over HTTP (`src/WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs:34`, `src/WebApp/Extensions/Extensions.cs:38`)
- **WebhookClient → Webhooks.API** over HTTP (`src/WebhookClient/Extensions/Extensions.cs:19`)
- Everything else is asynchronous over RabbitMQ — 13 integration events, all cross-service. The core saga is Ordering.API → Catalog.API for stock validation (`src/Ordering.API/Application/DomainEventHandlers/OrderStatusChangedToAwaitingValidationDomainEventHandler.cs:33`), Ordering.API → PaymentProcessor (`src/Ordering.API/Application/DomainEventHandlers/OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedDomainEventHandler.cs:30`), and back (`src/PaymentProcessor/IntegrationEvents/EventHandling/OrderStatusChangedToStockConfirmedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:27`).
- The only hosted background loop is **GracePeriodManagerService** in OrderProcessor (`src/OrderProcessor/Extensions/Extensions.cs:18`), which publishes `GracePeriodConfirmedIntegrationEvent` to Ordering.API (`src/OrderProcessor/Services/GracePeriodManagerService.cs:55`).

Across the whole solution the analyzer counts **109 entry points**: 43 HTTP endpoints, 42 UI entries, 13 message consumers, 7 domain event handlers, 3 gRPC methods (`Basket.GetBasket`, `Basket.UpdateBasket`, `Basket.DeleteBasket`, all at `src/Basket.API/Grpc/BasketService.cs:8`), and 1 hosted service.
